claims.text: The starting material is a laser-powder-bed-fused refractory MoNbTaW high-entropy alloy.
The as-fabricated MoNbTaW alloy has a disordered or random solid-solution microstructure.
A short-duration vacuum anneal near 1000°C can induce short-range chemical order in laser-powder-bed-fused MoNbTaW.
Approximately 5 minutes near 1000°C is a candidate annealing condition for producing beneficial short-range order.
The anneal produces nanoscale short-range-ordered domains within the disordered matrix.
Limited short-range order increases edge-dislocation mobility in MoNbTaW.
Limited short-range order moderates screw-dislocation activity in MoNbTaW.
The proposed changes in edge- and screw-dislocation behavior enhance plasticity and make deformation more uniform.
Beneficial short-range order can improve plasticity without diminishing lattice strength.
The annealed alloy will have greater tensile ductility than the untreated alloy.
The annealed alloy will have greater compressive ductility than the untreated alloy.
The annealed alloy will undergo more uniform plastic deformation during dynamic loading than the untreated alloy.
The annealed alloy will retain the high yield strength of the untreated alloy.
The annealed alloy will maintain or enhance impact-induced energy release relative to the untreated alloy.
Over-aging may adversely affect the balance between ductility and strength.
Oxidation during processing could limit the benefits of the annealing treatment.
The proposed effect may not transfer to MoNbTaW made by fabrication methods other than laser powder bed fusion.
